text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- Varujan Vosganian, head of the Senate budget, finance and banking commission, lists six priority targets which Romania should attain in order to develop its capital markets.
ECONOMISTUL
- The present fiscal and budget policy of harnessing inflation is counter-productive and might lead to economic collapse, the newspaper says.
- The way in which profit tax is calculated in Romania, according to the laws in force, applies to an imaginary, not to a real profit, the newspaper says.
ADEVARUL:
- The Romanian flagship carrier Tarom will keep only 23 aircraft in its fleet, the newspaper says of the company's restructuring which the government and the State Ownership Fund announced on Monday.
- How will farmers be able to harvest this year's bumper grain crop? -- newspaper survey of rising prices for harvesters.
- "Inter-enterprise arrears have increased...we have exceeded the forecast budget gap for the first four months," Industry and Trade Minister Calin Popescu Tariceanu said.
LIBERTATEA
- Wheat, maize, sunflower seeds and oil, as well as snails export was liberalised starting Monday.
- Romanian oil refineries will stand on their own feet after June 30, says newspaper report on restructuring of Romanian Oil Company, which will involve 200 layoffs.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Foreigners need a work permit in order to be employed in Romania, according to a recent government decision.
General:
ADEVARUL
- The lower Chamber of Deputies will vote today on whether to strip Gabriel Bivolaru, of the leftist opposition Party of Social Democracy, of his immunity over fraud suspicions.
LIBERTATEA
- Ruling coalition leaders don't want parliament to go into summer recess at the end of June, the paper says.
- The last no-confidence motion fuelled a competition of jokes in parliament.
- Romanian wine tasters say that the best domestic wines are sweet ones, says newspaper report.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- "Wounded, crippled, forgotten -- the children of the revolution," newspaper reports on the fate of teenagers who rebelled against communism in Romania's 1989 revolution, ahead of proposed merger of anti-communist revolutionaries' groups.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264
